title: Payments with a paper trail.
lede: PulsePay brings merchant billing, treasury controls and native agent payments into one TypeScript workspace. Each chain has an explicit job and its own verification path.

title: Your first confirmed payment.
lede: Build the workspace, configure the merchant hub, then open a real invoice in the React checkout. The amount comes from the contract.

title: Use and test the merchant console.
lede: Every console control, merchant and customer payment tests, refunds, and the current limits of subscription, agent and bridge flows.

title: Three tracks. Explicit boundaries.
lede: Follow value and evidence separately: contract state, transaction receipts, challenge redemption and audit consensus each answer a different question.

title: Install PulsePay with NPX
lede: Equip Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Copilot, or Antigravity with the PulsePay Agent Skill using NPX.

title: One contract for the merchant ledger.
lede: PulsePayMerchantHub stores invoices, payments, subscription plans and per-merchant balances on Whitechain Sepolia.

title: An invoice is a contract record.
lede: Create an amount, a due time and an optional customer restriction. Discover the ID from InvoiceCreated and read its current state before payment.

title: Settlement needs evidence.
lede: A wallet approval is not a payment. PulsePay reports checkout success after the hub emits a matching PaymentSettled event in a successful receipt.

title: Refund to the original payer.
lede: The reserve backs full and partial refunds against an actual settled invoice. Every refund produces a transaction and cumulative accounting evidence.

title: A plan. A consent. Each cycle.
lede: Plans define amount, interval and maximum cycles. Subscribers authorize a plan; eligible renewals settle with an explicit renewal ID.

title: A ledger your accountant can read.
lede: Export actual payment and refund events with UTC timestamps, raw units and transaction evidence using the shared workspace formatter.

title: Cross-Chain Token Bridging with CCIP 2.0.
lede: Bridge tokens across Ethereum Sepolia and Hedera Testnet via official CCIP Routers with 0-gas destination callbacks.

title: Agents pay in HBAR. Nobody approves.
lede: An agent discovers a service, clears its spend policy, answers a 402 challenge and settles in native HBAR. The worker writes an audit trail to consensus.

title: Decide before the transfer.
lede: PulsePaySpendLimitPolicy validates tool and merchant permissions and reserves a bounded transfer budget before the worker spends.

title: A payment and its audit are different records.
lede: PulsePayHcsAuditHook records settled agent actions on the configured HCS topic. Failed audit submission is retryable without paying again.

title: Plug policy and audit into the worker.
lede: PulsePayHederaPlugin binds native HBAR payment and refund tools to the supplied Agent Kit context and its seven-stage lifecycle.

title: A checkout that reads the invoice.
lede: Wrap the checkout with PulsePayProvider. Supply the deployed merchant hub and let the widget read the amount, request the wallet and verify settlement.

title: One client. Explicit adapters.
lede: createPulsePay constructs Whitechain, quote routing and optional treasury adapters and exposes their real methods through typed groups.

title: The receipt is checked on the server.
lede: The server SDK publishes service terms and gates paid API responses on independently verified native Hedera receipts.

title: Deployed interfaces, without guessed addresses.
lede: The repository contains merchant billing and treasury contracts. Deployment addresses are environment configuration, not constants invented by the website.

title: Configuration follows the trust boundary.
lede: Public chain addresses may reach the browser. API credentials, signing keys, challenge state and service secrets stay on the server.

title: A failed read stays a failed read.
lede: The interface keeps the last request’s error visible and provides a retry. It never fills an unavailable chain with demonstration activity.

title: Verify the behavior. Share the evidence.
lede: Use the repository’s test and feedback records to make reproducible reports with a route, chain, transaction and expected outcome.
